sourceReview: Read bundled BSB Psalm 90 in full with each verse's related passages before drafting. References are thematic or literary comparisons, not an invented historical occasion. Scripture is never stored in the notes; it loads from the bundled BSB.

study.title: Teach us to number our days
study.intro: Moses, the man of God, sets the shortness of human life against God's eternity, confesses that sin brings God's anger, and asks God to teach His people wisdom, satisfy them with His love and establish the work of their hands.
study.context: Psalm 90 is headed 'A prayer of Moses the man of God,' making it likely the oldest psalm. It opens Book IV of the Psalms, which answers the crisis of Psalm 89 by turning back to God as the eternal King and refuge from before Israel had kings. Verses 1-2 praise God's eternity; verses 3-12 reflect on human frailty and sin; verses 13-17 plead for compassion, joy and lasting work. Many read it against the forty years of wandering, when a whole generation died in the wilderness.
study.peopleNote: The heading names Moses the man of God, so Moses is linked. Jesus, the eternal Word who shared our short human life and brings lasting joy, is linked. God is never portrayed as a human body in planned art.

verses.title: Our dwelling place
verses.heading: A home through every generation
verses.meaning: The heading calls this 'A prayer of Moses the man of God.' Moses spent forty years leading a homeless people through the wilderness, yet he begins, 'Lord, You have been our dwelling place through all generations.' Israel had tents, not houses, and no land of its own yet. Their true home was God Himself. Every generation, from Abraham onward, had found shelter in Him. That is still true for His people wherever they live.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 33:1 calls Moses 'the man of God' as he blesses Israel. Deuteronomy 33:27 says, 'The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.' John 15:4 records Jesus saying, 'Remain in Me, and I will remain in you.'
explore: Man of God
A title for a prophet who speaks for God, used of Moses, Samuel, Elijah and others.
Dwelling place
A home or refuge where one lives and is sheltered, here God Himself.
verses.reflect: When life feels unsettled, how can you make God your true home today?
verses.alt: A cluster of tents stands in a wide desert valley under evening light.

verses.title: Before the mountains
verses.heading: From everlasting to everlasting
verses.meaning: Verse 2 reaches back before creation: 'Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.' Mountains seem the oldest, most permanent things on earth, yet God was there before them. The words 'born' and 'brought forth' picture creation as a birth. God has no beginning and no end. Everything else is young next to Him.
verses.context: Genesis 1:1 says, 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.' Proverbs 8:25 speaks of wisdom present before the mountains were settled. John 1:1-2 says the Word was with God in the beginning.
explore: Everlasting
Without beginning or end, stretching endlessly in both directions of time.
Brought forth
Gave birth to or produced, here describing God creating the world.
verses.reflect: How does God's eternity put your present worries into perspective?
verses.alt: Ancient mountain ranges stretch to the horizon under a dawn sky.

verses.title: Return to dust
verses.heading: Mortals called back
verses.meaning: 'You return man to dust, saying, Return, O sons of mortals.' Moses echoes Genesis 3:19, where God told Adam, 'For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.' Humans are made from the ground and go back to it at God's word. The contrast with verse 2 is sharp: God is everlasting, we are dust. This is not despair but realism, the first step toward wisdom.
verses.context: Genesis 3:19 says, 'For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.' Ecclesiastes 12:7 says the dust returns to the ground and the spirit returns to God. Psalm 103:14 says God remembers that we are dust.
explore: Dust
Fine dry earth, a picture of human frailty and our origin from the ground.
Mortals
Human beings who are subject to death, in contrast to the eternal God.
verses.reflect: How might remembering that you are dust make you more humble and more dependent on God?
verses.alt: A handful of dry earth slips through open fingers in sunlight.

verses.title: A thousand years as a day
verses.heading: God's view of time
verses.meaning: Verse 4 says, 'For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night.' What seems an age to us is like yesterday to God. A watch of the night was a few hours, often slept through. Time does not wear God down or limit Him. Peter would later use this verse to explain why God's patience is not slowness.
verses.context: 2 Peter 3:8-9 says with the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and He is patient, not wanting anyone to perish. Psalm 102:27 says, 'You remain the same, and Your years will never end.' Isaiah 40:28 says the everlasting God does not grow tired.
explore: Watch of the night
One of the divisions of the night, a few hours long, when guards kept watch.
In Your sight
From God's point of view, as He sees and measures things.
verses.reflect: How does knowing God sees time differently help you wait for His answers?
verses.alt: A night watchman stands on a city wall under the stars with a small lamp.

verses.title: Swept away in sleep
verses.heading: Lives carried off like a flood
verses.meaning: 'You sweep them away in their sleep; they are like the new grass of the morning.' Human generations pass as if swept away by a flood or as quickly as a dream ends at waking. The image shifts to grass, which fills the next verse. In the dry lands of the Bible, grass sprang up fresh after dew or rain, yet it never lasted long. Life is real, but fragile.
verses.context: Job 14:1-2 says man springs up like a flower and withers. Isaiah 40:6-8 says all people are like grass, but the word of our God stands forever. James 4:14 says, 'You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.'
explore: Sweep away
To carry off suddenly and completely, as floodwaters wash things away.
New grass
Fresh green growth that springs up after rain or dew, short-lived in a dry land.
verses.reflect: How does knowing life is fragile change the way you treat the people around you today?
verses.alt: Fresh green grass glistens with morning dew on a hillside.

verses.title: Fading by evening
verses.heading: Morning green, evening withered
verses.meaning: Verse 6 completes the picture: 'in the morning it springs up new, but by evening it fades and withers.' In the heat of a Middle Eastern day, fresh grass could wilt by sunset. That is how fast a human life seems from God's view. Moses watched a whole generation fall in the wilderness. Yet the psalm does not end here; it moves toward asking God to make our short days count.
verses.context: Psalm 103:15-16 says our days are like grass; the wind passes and it is gone. 1 Peter 1:24-25 quotes Isaiah: the grass withers, but the word of the Lord endures. Matthew 6:30 says God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and gone tomorrow.
explore: Fades
Loses color and freshness, growing pale and weak as the day goes on.
Withers
Dries up and shrivels, losing life as plants do in heat.
verses.reflect: What lasting things can you invest in, knowing that so much fades by evening?
verses.alt: Dry, wilted grass bends on a hillside at sunset.

verses.title: Consumed by anger
verses.heading: Mortality and God's wrath
verses.meaning: 'For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.' Moses connects human frailty with sin and God's judgment. Death is not merely natural; it entered the world through sin. In the wilderness, Israel's rebellion led to a whole generation dying before reaching Canaan. Moses saw it firsthand. To understand our shortness of life honestly is also to face God's holy displeasure at sin.
verses.context: Numbers 14:29 says the rebellious generation's bodies would fall in the wilderness. Romans 5:12 says death came into the world through sin. Romans 6:23 says the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life.
explore: Consumed
Used up or destroyed, as fire burns something away.
Wrath
God's settled, holy opposition to sin and to every form of evil.
verses.reflect: How does Romans 6:23 answer the problem of verse 7?
verses.alt: Wilderness graves of piled stones line a dry valley at dusk.

verses.title: Secret sins exposed
verses.heading: In the light of His face
verses.meaning: Verse 8 says, 'You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence.' Nothing is hidden from God. Sins we keep from others, and even from ourselves, lie open before Him. 'The light of Your presence' usually means blessing, but here it is searching light that reveals. This is frightening, but also the first step to real forgiveness, which only comes when sin is honestly faced.
verses.context: Hebrews 4:13 says nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight. Psalm 139:23-24 prays, 'Search me, O God.' 1 John 1:9 says if we confess our sins, He is faithful to forgive.
explore: Iniquities
Crooked or twisted wrongdoings, including their guilt.
Secret sins
Hidden faults known only to oneself, or not recognized even by oneself.
verses.reflect: Is there a hidden sin you need to bring into God's light so you can be forgiven?
verses.alt: Morning light falls through a doorway into a dark room, revealing its corners.

verses.title: Finished with a sigh
verses.heading: Years that decline
verses.meaning: 'For all our days decline in Your fury; we finish our years with a sigh.' Life under sin's shadow winds down like the day toward evening. A sigh is a faint breath, a moan or a passing thought. The years we thought so full end like a breath. Moses is not wallowing; he is naming the human condition honestly so that the prayer of verse 12 will make sense.
verses.context: Psalm 39:5 says each man's life is but a breath. Job 7:6 says, 'My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle.' Ecclesiastes 1:2 begins, 'Futility of futilities.'
explore: Decline
To go down or sink, like the sun lowering toward evening.
Sigh
A faint breath or murmur, here describing how quickly a life ends.
verses.reflect: What would you want to be said about your life when your years are finished?
verses.alt: An old man sits on a bench watching the sun set over fields.

verses.title: Seventy years
verses.heading: Labor, sorrow and flight
verses.meaning: Verse 10 says, 'The length of our days is seventy years, or eighty if we are strong; yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away.' Even a long life is short. Its best parts, its 'pride,' still involve toil and trouble. Then life flies away like a bird. Moses himself lived to 120, but he knew most did not. Every life is brief compared with God.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 34:7 says Moses was 120 years old when he died. 2 Samuel 19:35 records Barzillai at eighty saying he could no longer enjoy life's pleasures. 2 Corinthians 4:16-18 says our light, momentary troubles are achieving an eternal glory.
explore: Pride
Here the best or proudest part of life, its strength and achievements.
Fly away
To pass quickly like a bird taking flight, a picture of death.
verses.reflect: How does 2 Corinthians 4:17 change the way you see labor and sorrow?
verses.alt: A flock of birds lifts off from a field and flies into the evening sky.

verses.title: Who knows Your anger?
verses.heading: Fear matching His holiness
verses.meaning: 'Who knows the power of Your anger? Your wrath matches the fear You are due.' Few people take God's holiness seriously. His anger against sin is as great as the reverence He deserves, and He deserves infinite reverence. Moses is not describing a temper but a holy God. To grasp this leads not to terror alone but to wisdom: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
verses.context: Proverbs 9:10 says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. Hebrews 10:31 says it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. Luke 12:4-5 records Jesus saying to fear the One who has authority over life and death.
explore: Fear
Reverent awe and respect for God's holiness and power.
Due
Owed or deserved, what is rightly fitting to give to someone worthy.
verses.reflect: How does a right fear of God lead to wisdom rather than anxiety?
verses.alt: Lightning flashes over a vast mountain range at night.

verses.title: Number our days
verses.heading: A heart of wisdom
verses.meaning: Verse 12 is the psalm's turning point: 'So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.' To number our days is to count them as precious and few. This is not morbid; it is clarity. When we remember life is short, we stop wasting it on what does not matter. The goal is a wise heart presented to God, like an offering.
verses.context: Ephesians 5:15-16 urges, 'Be very careful how you walk... redeeming the time.' Psalm 39:4 prays, 'Show me, O LORD, my end and the measure of my days.' James 1:5 says if anyone lacks wisdom, he should ask God.
explore: Number
To count carefully, treating each item as valuable and limited.
Heart of wisdom
An inner life shaped by God's truth so that choices reflect His ways.
verses.reflect: If you counted your remaining days as precious, what would you start or stop doing?
verses.alt: A notched wooden tally stick lies beside an hourglass on a table.

verses.title: Return, O LORD
verses.heading: Compassion on servants
verses.meaning: 'Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.' The word 'return' echoes verse 3, where God tells mortals to return to dust. Now Moses asks God Himself to return, to turn back toward His people in mercy. 'How long' is a cry of faith. Moses appeals to God's compassion, the tender love of a father for his children.
verses.context: Exodus 32:12 records Moses praying, 'Turn from Your fierce anger; relent from this disaster.' Psalm 103:13 says as a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion. Joel 2:13 says, 'Return to the LORD your God, for He is gracious and compassionate.'
explore: Compassion
Tender, caring love that is moved by another's suffering.
Servants
Those who belong to and serve a master, here God's people.
verses.reflect: What area of your life would you ask God to return to with His compassion?
verses.alt: A father runs down a dusty road toward a returning figure.

verses.title: Satisfied in the morning
verses.heading: Joy all our days
verses.meaning: Verse 14 asks, 'Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.' After the night of judgment comes the hope of morning. Moses asks God to fill His people with His steadfast love, as the manna filled them each morning in the wilderness. That love would make even short lives full of joy.
verses.context: Exodus 16:21 says each morning the people gathered manna. Lamentations 3:22-23 says God's mercies are new every morning. John 6:35 records Jesus saying, 'I am the bread of life.'
explore: Satisfy
To fill completely so that hunger or longing is met.
Loving devotion
God's steadfast covenant love, loyal and kind, which He never abandons.
verses.reflect: What would it look like to start each morning asking God to satisfy you with His love?
verses.alt: Morning sunlight falls on white flakes covering the ground in a desert camp.

verses.title: Gladness to match
verses.heading: Joy for years of affliction
verses.meaning: 'Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.' Moses asks for joy proportional to sorrow. If Israel endured forty years in the wilderness, let there be at least as many years of gladness. It is a bold, honest request. God's restoration is generous, often outweighing the suffering that came before.
verses.context: Joel 2:25 promises, 'I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts.' Romans 8:18 says present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory to be revealed. Job 42:12 says the LORD blessed Job's latter days more than his first.
explore: Afflicted
Weighed down by suffering, illness or hardship over time.
Gladness
Deep joy and contentment that fills the heart and overflows in song.
verses.reflect: Can you ask God to restore joy in proportion to a season of sorrow you have known?
verses.alt: A family dances at harvest time in a field of golden grain.

verses.title: Work and splendor shown
verses.heading: For children to see
verses.meaning: Verse 16 prays, 'May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.' Moses wants God's mighty acts to be seen by his generation and God's glory by the next. The wilderness generation saw judgment; he longs for their children to see glory. Every parent and leader can pray this: that those who follow us will see God's power and beauty.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 6:6-7 says to teach God's words diligently to your children. Psalm 78:4 says, 'We will not hide them from their children.' 2 Timothy 1:5 recalls the sincere faith passed from Lois to Eunice to Timothy.
explore: Splendor
Brilliant glory and majesty that inspires wonder in all who see it.
Work
God's mighty deeds and saving acts done for His people.
verses.reflect: Who in the next generation can you pray will see God's splendor?
verses.alt: A grandparent points out the night stars to a small child.

verses.title: Establish our work
verses.heading: Favor resting upon us
verses.meaning: The psalm closes: 'May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish for us the work of our hands, yes, establish the work of our hands!' Life is short, but work done under God's favor can last. To establish is to make firm and permanent. The repetition shows Moses' longing. Ordinary daily labor, offered to God, can have lasting value beyond our brief years.
verses.context: 1 Corinthians 15:58 says your labor in the Lord is not in vain. Colossians 3:23 says, 'Whatever you do, work at it with your whole heart, as working for the Lord.' Psalm 127:1 says unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain.
explore: Favor
God's gracious kindness and approval, freely given and resting on His people.
Establish
To make firm and lasting so that it endures beyond the moment.
verses.reflect: What work are you doing this week that you can offer to God, asking Him to establish it?
verses.alt: Hands shape clay on a potter's wheel in a workshop lit by morning sun.
